entries.label: estimated
entries.why: Explained. Cell G_STA <- E_BANK: 84,959 -> 29,316 (-55,643, -65.5%; 3 entries). Largest moves: fincorp R4 deposits -54,971 (-65.5%); fincorp R4 borrowings -671 (-65.5%). The largest mover is explained under its entry: GG interest received from banks is FSF deposit and loan stocks x the scaled cost of deposits (low). No bridge sees such a receipt: the States' interest receipts (28,494) are booked in R7x from E_NFPU, and the 4,620 urban local bodies report interest income of only 3,158 (FC16 cityfinance; government-26). With G_STA's prior excess (4,50,426) and E_BANK's deficit (-1,02,838), balancing cut it toward that evidence.

entries.label: balancing_set

The published line (government-32) is held within 5% by gov.r7x.g_sta.mining_royalties and each payer sector's part within 25% of its key share by the Wave C payer bands; the key is a proxy (NAS 2026 St 7.1A/7.1B/7.1C OS(+MI) + CFC of the industry; government-23). entries.label: balancing_set
entries.why: Explained. G_STA <- F_GOSC F4b total, 2,64,607 -> 2,59,053 (-5,554, -2.1%; z 0.979; free medium; binding: f4.gg_gos (target 3,75,679, balanced 3,75,679, at its lower edge)). F4b splits GG GOS (= NAS GG CFC, held by f4.gg_gos) by NAS 2026 St 4.1 NVA; no clean source splits GG CFC by government (factors-15). The Centre/State gap of distributive flows (G_CEN -2,98,948, G_STA 4,50,426; government-27) pulls the Centre's receipt up; the Wave C band f4b.centre (target 1,11,072, balanced 1,16,625, at its upper edge) (audit BS-12) now stops it at +5% of the NVA key (the earlier run reached a Centre share of 0.323 against 0.296). C2a still moves own output to the States within its own +-10% band on cash evidence, so the two splits built from one key differ by up to those bands (BS-12, accepted and documented in factors-22). GRAS (no weights, no constraints) gives 2,20,199.

entries.label: official
entries.why: Explained (a compensating move, bounded; government-34). Cell G_STA <- G_CEN: 17,80,541 -> 17,45,667 (-34,874, -2.0%; 14 entries). Largest moves: government R2 css_outside_treasury -28,561 (-19.2%); fincorp R3 gsec_state_reserve_funds -3,965 (-21.4%); government R2 css_and_other -2,319 (-1.1%); fincorp R3 itb_14d -30 (-1.5%). The prior books the Centre's CSS money released outside State treasuries (Union Budget St 18 III CSS revenue 4,25,296 less MH 3601.06 net releases 2,57,208 = 1,68,087; D2-8, government-6) as a G_STA receipt, but no block writes the outside-treasury agencies' spending, so it adds to G_STA's 4,50,426 excess and the Centre's -2,98,948 shortfall. The Wave C band gov.r2.css_outside_treasury (target 1,68,087, balanced 1,51,279, at its lower edge) now holds the transfer (current + capital) within 10% of the published derivation (IGAS-2 'Others' grantees 1,73,699 is within 3.3%), so balancing could cut it only to the band edge (current + capital 1,51,279, -10%) instead of the -38.8% of the earlier run; the rest of the States' excess left through the saving split (K3a).
